Balanced but more cautious: The FOMC notes strong labor markets and low unemployment, with inflation below 2% and soft business fixed investment—supporting a hold with a dovish bias. The April 2019 SLOOS tilts the outlook more cautious: banks tightened standards for C&I and construction/land development loans and tightened other terms broadly; demand was weaker for construction/land development loans and multiple consumer categories (HELOCs, credit cards, other consumer), with demand roughly unchanged for auto and subprime mortgages. These tighter credit conditions and weaker loan demand are consistent with softer capex and could restrain consumer credit, reinforcing the Fed’s risk‑management stance and Bullard’s dissent in favor of an insurance cut.

Net tone: mildly positive on current conditions, but more cautious on the outlook and credit channel. Adjusting for SLOOS, the overall sentiment edges closer to neutral from the prior mildly positive read.
